# package sks

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-opcua/pubsub/sks"
```

Package sks is the client side of the OPC UA PubSub Security Key Service (Part 14 §8): GetSecurityKeys and SetSecurityKeys calls, a KeySource that pulls the keys of a SecurityGroup from an SKS and keeps them fresh, and a helper that pushes the keys of a local KeyService to a Publisher or Subscriber.

```go
	DefaultMaxRetry = 30 * time.Second
	DefaultTimeout  = 30 * time.Second
)
```

Defaults of Config.

```go
const DefaultPullInterval = time.Second
```

DefaultPullInterval is how often a Puller reads the configuration of its runtime by default.

## Variables

```go
var ErrBadResponse = errors.New("pubsub/sks: malformed GetSecurityKeys response")
```

ErrBadResponse is returned for a GetSecurityKeys response that does not have the output arguments of the method.

```go
var ErrEndpoint = errors.New("pubsub/sks: no SKS to pull keys from")
```

ErrEndpoint is in the chain of the error of EndpointDialer.Dial for an EndpointDescription that names no SKS to pull keys from: nil, without a Server, an ApplicationType other than SERVER (the push model), or without a URL (Part 14 §6.2.5.4 Table 40).

## Functions

### func Push

```go
func Push(ctx context.Context, ks *security.KeyService, c *opcua.Client, securityGroupID string) error
```

Push sends the current and all future keys of a SecurityGroup of a local KeyService to the server c is connected to with SetSecurityKeys. Call it again after every key change (KeyLifetime) to keep the target supplied.

### func SetSecurityKeys

```go
func SetSecurityKeys(ctx context.Context, c *opcua.Client, securityGroupID string, keys *Result) error
```

SetSecurityKeys calls PublishSubscribe.SetSecurityKeys (i=17364) on the Publisher or Subscriber c is connected to, pushing keys for a SecurityGroup: keys.Keys\[0] is the current key with token id keys.FirstTokenID, the rest are future keys.

### type EndpointDialer

```go
type EndpointDialer struct {
	// Options are the options of every client: the certificate, key and
	// trust of the application and the user identity the SKS grants

	Options []opcua.Option

```

EndpointDialer opens a session with the SKS an element of the SecurityKeyServices of a PubSubGroup or DataSetReader describes (Part 14 §6.2.5.4 Table 40): GetEndpoints on its Server.DiscoveryUrls in order, the SignAndEncrypt endpoint of its SecurityPolicyUri (the best policy both support when it is empty), and a check that the endpoint has the ApplicationUri of its Server, the main key of the SKS. Table 40 leaves the EndpointUrl empty; one that is set is tried when there are no DiscoveryUrls (a tolerance).

### type KeySource

```go
type KeySource struct {

	// last Refresh triggered by an unknown token

}
```

KeySource is a security.KeySource for one SecurityGroup that pulls the keys from an SKS with GetSecurityKeys. It fetches the keys once in NewKeySource and then in the background: right after the key change that leaves the source with at most one future key, so that whenever the SKS hands out future keys a fetch has two key lifetimes to complete before the source runs out of keys. A received message with a token just ahead of the current one that the source does not hold (the peer fetched first) triggers a fetch too, at most once per MinRetry. Failed fetches are retried with exponential backoff. Close stops it.

A fetch returns the current key and the future keys, not the past ones: a subscriber whose first fetch comes just after a key change does not hold the previous key, and rejects the messages that a publisher which has not changed keys yet still secures with it (at most the publisher's response delay). Where a publisher and a subscriber start together, create the subscriber's KeySource first.

### type Puller

```go
type Puller struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

Puller supplies the keys of the secured groups of a PubSub runtime that pull them from an SKS (Part 14 §5.4.5.3, Figure 11): for every SecurityGroupId of a WriterGroup, ReaderGroup or DataSetReader with SecurityMode Sign or SignAndEncrypt whose SecurityKeyServices name an SKS with ApplicationType SERVER (the pull model, §6.2.5.4 Table 40), and whose keys the runtime has from no other source, it starts a KeySource on the first SKS that answers and sets it in the runtime (PubSub.SetKeySource). A first fetch that fails on every SKS is tried again with backoff (OPC 10000-81 E.5: the AutomationComponent retries with vendor-specific logic); until then the groups have no keys, which leaves them without secured messages (§5.4.5.3: PreOperational). When the configuration no longer has the SecurityGroupId, the Puller removes its KeySource from the runtime and closes it. A KeySource it set stays with the SKS it was started on while the group is configured.

#### func NewPuller

```go
func NewPuller(rt *pubsub.PubSub, opts PullerOptions) (*Puller, error)
```

NewPuller starts a Puller on rt. It reads the configuration at once and then every Interval; Close stops it.

#### func (Puller) Close

```go
func (p *Puller) Close() error
```

Close stops the Puller: the fetches in progress are cancelled, and the KeySources it set are removed from the runtime and closed.


SecurityGroups returns the SecurityGroupIds the Puller supplies keys for, sorted.

#### func (Puller) Sync

```go
func (p *Puller) Sync()
```

Sync reads the configuration of the runtime now: it starts the fetches of the SecurityGroups that need keys and drops the KeySources of those that are gone.

### type Result

#### func GetSecurityKeys

```go
func GetSecurityKeys(ctx context.Context, c *opcua.Client, securityGroupID string, startingTokenID, requestedKeyCount uint32) (*Result, error)
```

GetSecurityKeys calls PublishSubscribe.GetSecurityKeys (i=15215) on the SKS c is connected to. startingTokenID 0 asks for the current key; requestedKeyCount is the number of future keys wanted (the SKS caps it). The SKS only answers over a SignAndEncrypt session. A Bad method result is returned as an error wrapping the ua.StatusCode.
